method: Read-only source review and eight exact-history Regicide UCI queries, each depth cap 7 and node cap 1000000. Two forced-child depth-4 CLI queries confirm the fork fixture. No external engine move selection or production edits.
observations: Games 2 and 6 reach identical critical positions and continue with matching candidate moves and evaluation drops; these losses are not independent failure patterns.
No check-evasion or mate handling error found in the reviewed qsearch: checked nodes do not stand pat, all legal evasions are searched, mate takes precedence over draw counters.
Quiescence extends captures and promotions only. Quiet checks, quiet forks and other threats beyond the full-search horizon are not extended.

Evaluation has material, piece position, phase blending and home-minor development only. It does not compute attacked squares, king-zone danger, pawn structure, passed pawns or trapped-piece mobility.

An unfinished iterative depth is discarded in full, retaining the previous completed iteration. This preserves the current correctness contract, but tactical positions sometimes complete only depth 2 or 3 inside the recorded 80ms internal allowance.

reproducible_fork_fixture.interpretation: Quiet ...Ng4 threatens ...Nxf2, forking the queen on d3 and rook on d1. This fixture supports a tactical horizon failure, with the deeper own-engine alternative preventing the exchange loss. It does not by itself prove a general king-danger evaluation patch is best.

limits: Own-engine evaluation is not an independent oracle. Only the game13 fork is supported by matched child-depth comparison here. No matches or strength claims were made.
